# UI reference

The components that set up a screen, the icon set asset, the bases for your own HUD panels and windows, the presenters that read units for them, and the theme, icon and tooltip API. For how to use it, see [UI](../modules/ui.md).

## VtUiRoot

Component. Add it with **Add Component → Vantage → UI → VtUiRoot**. Adds `UIDocument` automatically.

The root of a screen's UI: six layers in a fixed order on the UI Document, so nameplates stay under the HUD, windows over it, menus over windows, dialogs and toasts over menus, and the tooltip in front of everything, whichever order components add themselves in. Every layer fills the screen and ignores the pointer itself, so clicks between panels reach the game.

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `static VtUiRoot Current { get; }` | The root in the loaded scene, or null. Cached until it goes away. |
| `bool IsBuilt { get; }` | Whether the layers exist on the UI Document's current root. |
| `event Action RootRebuilt` | Fires after the UI Document rebuilt its root and the layers were built again. Anything added to a layer before is gone; add it again here. |
| `const string LayerUssClassName` | Class on every layer. |
| `const string LayersUssClassName` | Class on the element holding the six layers. |
| `const string RegionUssClassName` | Class on every region. |
| `static string ClassName(VtUiLayer value)` | The class for `value`, such as `vt-layer--hud`. |
| `static string ClassName(VtUiRegion value)` | The class for `value`, such as `vt-region--top-left`. |
| `VisualElement Layer(VtUiLayer value)` | The element for `value`, or null while the UI Document has no panel settings. |
| `VisualElement Region(VtUiRegion value)` | The element for `value` on the HUD layer, created on first use, or null while the UI Document has no panel settings. Children stack in a column; top regions stack down, bottom ones up. |

## VtUiNavigation

Component. Add it with **Add Component → Vantage → UI → VtUiNavigation**.

The stack of open screens: windows, menus and dialogs. Push a screen to open it on top, and the Cancel input, Esc or the gamepad's east button, pops the top one, so every window closes the same way. While anything is open the player's gameplay input is held, so a key that opens a bag does not also cast, and focus moves to the screen that just opened and back to the one below when it closes.

### Inspector fields

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Block Gameplay While Open (`blockGameplayWhileOpen`) | `bool` | On | Hold the player's gameplay input (hotkeys, orders, selection, click-to-move) while a screen is open. |
| Hide Cursor On Gamepad (`hideCursorOnGamepad`) | `bool` | Off | Hide the mouse cursor while a screen is open and the player is on a gamepad. |

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `static VtUiNavigation Current { get; }` | The navigation in the loaded scene, or null. |
| `VisualElement Top { get; }` | The screen on top, or null. |
| `int Depth { get; }` | How many screens are open. |
| `bool IsOpen { get; }` | Whether any screen is open. |
| `bool BlockGameplayWhileOpen { get; set; }` | Whether gameplay input is held while a screen is open. |
| `event Action Changed` | Fires after a screen was pushed or popped. |
| `bool Contains(VisualElement screen)` | Whether `screen` is somewhere on the stack. |
| `void Push(VisualElement screen)` | Open `screen` on top. A screen already on the stack moves to the top. A `VtWindow` is opened; a `VtDialog` is left as it is, since `VtDialog.Show` shows it. |
| `void Open(VtWindow window, VtUiLayer layer = VtUiLayer.Windows)` | Put `window` on `layer` of the root when it has no parent yet, then push it. |
| `bool Pop()` | Close the top screen. False when nothing is open or the top is a blocking dialog. |
| `bool Close(VisualElement screen)` | Close `screen` wherever it is on the stack. False when it is not open. |
| `void Toggle(VtWindow window)` | Open `window` when it is closed, close it when it is open. |
| `void Clear()` | Close every screen, bottom to top. |

## VtTooltipHost

Component. Add it with **Add Component → Vantage → UI → VtTooltipHost**.

Puts the screen's one `VtTooltip` on the tooltip layer of the `VtUiRoot` and hands it to `VtTooltips.Host`, so every element attached with `VtTooltips.Attach` shows its tooltip there. Add it next to the root; without it tooltips are silently off.

### Inspector fields

| Field | Type | Default | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Delay Ms (`delayMs`) | `int` | 400 | ≥ 0 | Milliseconds the pointer or the focus rests on an element before its tooltip shows. |

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `VtTooltip Tooltip { get; }` | The tooltip element, or null before it is built. |

## VtMapArea

Component. Add it with **Add Component → Vantage → UI → VtMapArea**.

A stretch of ground a minimap can draw, read through `VtMinimapPresenter`: its size on the XZ plane around this object, the picture of it and the name the minimap shows while the player is inside.

### Inspector fields

#### General

| Field | Type | Default | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Size (`size`) | `Vector2` | (64, 64) |  | Width (world X) and depth (world Z) of the area in metres, centred on this object. |
| Image (`image`) | `Texture2D` | None |  | Top-down picture of the area with north up. Empty draws the minimap's plain background. |
| Display Name (`displayName`) | `string` | Empty |  | The area's name on the minimap, a localization key or plain text. Empty shows no name. |

#### Capture

| Field | Type | Default | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Capture Resolution (`captureResolution`) | `int` | 1024 | 128 to 4096 | Width in pixels of a captured image; the height follows the area's proportions. |
| Capture Layers (`captureLayers`) | `LayerMask` | Everything |  | Layers the capture camera renders. |
| Capture Background (`captureBackground`) | `Color` | `#17171CFF` |  | Colour where the capture sees nothing. |
| Capture Without Units (`captureWithoutUnits`) | `bool` | On |  | Leave units out of the capture, so the picture shows the ground and not who stood on it. |

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `static IReadOnlyList<VtMapArea> All { get; }` | Every enabled area. |
| `Vector2 Size { get; set; }` | Width (world X) and depth (world Z) in metres. |
| `Texture2D Image { get; set; }` | The top-down picture, north up, or null. |
| `string DisplayName { get; set; }` | The area's name, a localization key or plain text. |
| `int CaptureResolution { get; set; }` | Width in pixels of a captured image. |
| `Rect WorldRect { get; }` | The area on the XZ plane: `x`/`y` are the world X and Z of its minimum corner. |
| `bool Contains(Vector3 world)` | Whether `world` lies inside the area, ignoring height. |
| `static VtMapArea Find(Vector3 world)` | The smallest enabled area holding `world`, or null. |
| `Texture2D Capture()` | Render the area from straight above into a new texture, `CaptureResolution` wide, with the capture settings of this area. The caller owns the texture. Set it as `Image` to use it. |

## VtMapMarker

Component. Add it with **Add Component → Vantage → UI → VtMapMarker**.

Puts an icon on the minimap at this object, read through `VtMinimapPresenter`: a vendor, a dungeon entrance, a waypoint. On a unit it replaces the unit's dot.

### Inspector fields

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Icon (`icon`) | `string` | `"map-pin"` | Icon id from the icon set, such as store, flag or house. |
| Tint (`tint`) | [VtMapMarkerTint](#vtmapmarkertint) | `Foreground` | Colour of the icon. |
| Reveal (`reveal`) | [VtMapMarkerReveal](#vtmapmarkerreveal) | `WhenExplored` | When the marker shows through the fog of war. |
| Pin To Edge (`pinToEdge`) | `bool` | Off | Keep the marker on the rim of the minimap while it is out of range, pointing the way. |

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `static IReadOnlyList<VtMapMarker> All { get; }` | Every enabled marker. |
| `string Icon { get; set; }` | Icon id from the icon set. |
| `VtMapMarkerTint Tint { get; set; }` | Colour of the icon. |
| `VtMapMarkerReveal Reveal { get; set; }` | When the marker shows through the fog of war. |
| `bool PinToEdge { get; set; }` | Whether the marker stays on the rim of the minimap while out of range. |

## VtIconSet

Asset. Create it with **Create → Vantage → UI → Icon Set**.

The icons the UI refers to by id. The package ships one with the Lucide glyphs that its own components use; `VtIcons` looks ids up there. Make your own set for extra icons and install it with `VtIcons.Install`; set `fallback` to the shipped set, or leave it empty, and ids your set lacks still resolve through the shipped one.

### Inspector fields

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fallback (`fallback`) | [VtIconSet](#vticonset) | None | Looked up for ids this set does not have. |
| Entries (`entries`) | [VtIconEntry](#vticonentry)[] | Empty | One row per icon. |

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `int Count { get; }` | How many icons this set holds, without its fallback. |
| `bool TryGet(string id, out Background background)` | The image for `id` from this set or its fallbacks. False when no set has it. |
| `bool Contains(string id)` | Whether this set, or a fallback, has an icon called `id`. |
| `void Rebuild()` | Rebuild the lookup after editing `entries` at runtime. |

## VtHudPanel

Abstract component base.

Base of every HUD controller: builds its element once, puts it in a region of the `VtUiRoot` on the same object, or the scene's root, and builds it again when the UI Document rebuilds its root. Subclasses build in `Build` and refresh in `Refresh`, which runs every frame while the panel is shown.

### Inspector fields

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Region (`region`) | [VtUiRegion](#vtuiregion) | Where on the HUD the panel sits. |
| Order (`order`) | `int` | Where the panel sits among the others in its region: lower first, from the top of the region down. Panels with the same order keep the order they were built in. |
| Layout (`layout`) | `VisualTreeAsset` | A UXML layout of your own for this panel, with the same part names as the shipped one. Empty uses the shipped layout. |

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `VtUiRegion Region { get; set; }` | Where on the HUD the panel sits. Changing it moves the panel. |
| `int Order { get; set; }` | Where the panel sits among the others in its region: lower first, from the top of the region down. Panels with the same order keep the order they were built in. Changing it moves the panel. |
| `VisualTreeAsset Layout { get; set; }` | A UXML layout of your own for this panel, with the same part names as the shipped one. Null uses the shipped layout. Changing it builds the panel again. |
| `protected virtual string DefaultLayout { get; }` | The name of the shipped layout under `Resources/VtLayouts`, or null for a panel built in code. |
| `VisualElement Element { get; }` | The panel's element, or null before it is built. |
| `bool Hidden { get; set; }` | Whether the panel is hidden. A hidden panel keeps its element and stops refreshing. |
| `protected VtUiRoot Root { get; }` | The root this panel sits under, or null. |
| `protected VisualElement InstantiateLayout()` | Clone `Layout`, or the shipped `DefaultLayout` when none is set, and hand back its root element. Null when neither exists, so the panel draws nothing. |
| `void Toggle()` | Show or hide the panel. |
| `protected abstract VisualElement Build()` | Build the panel's element. Called once per root. |
| `protected abstract void Refresh()` | Update the element from the game. Runs every frame while the panel is shown. |
| `void PlaceIn(VisualElement container)` | Put the panel under `container`, an element of your own, instead of a region of the root. Null goes back to the region. The element is built again under the new parent. |
| `void RefreshNow()` | Draw the panel now, attaching it if needed, instead of waiting for the next frame, for example right after changing what it shows. |
| `protected bool EnsureAttached()` | Build the element now if it is not on screen yet. True when it is. |
| `protected void Detach()` | Take the element off screen and forget it. |

## VtWindowPanel

Abstract component base.

Base of every window controller: builds a `VtWindow` once on a layer of the `VtUiRoot`, opens and closes it through the `VtUiNavigation` when the scene has one, so Esc and the gamepad close it and gameplay input is held while it is open, and refreshes it every frame while it is open. Subclasses fill the window in `BuildContent` and update it in `Refresh`.

### Inspector fields

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Title (`title`) | `string` | The window's title, or its localization key. Empty uses the panel's own default. |
| Layer (`layer`) | [VtUiLayer](#vtuilayer) | Which layer of the root the window sits on. |
| Draggable (`draggable`) | `bool` | Let the player drag the window by its header. |
| Starts Open (`startsOpen`) | `bool` | Open the window as soon as the scene starts. |

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `VtWindow Window { get; }` | The window, or null before it is built. |
| `bool IsOpen { get; }` | Whether the window is open. |
| `protected abstract string DefaultTitle { get; }` | The title shown when the field is empty. |
| `protected VtUiRoot Root { get; }` | The root this window sits under, or null. |
| `protected VtUiNavigation Navigation { get; }` | The navigation stack windows open through, or null when the scene has none. |
| `protected abstract void BuildContent(VtWindow window)` | Fill `window` with the panel's content. Called once per build. |
| `protected abstract void Refresh()` | Update the content from the game. Runs on open and every frame while open. |
| `void Open()` | Open the window on top of the navigation stack, or on its own without one. |
| `void Close()` | Close the window. |
| `void Toggle()` | Open the window when it is closed, close it when it is open. |
| `void PlaceIn(VisualElement container)` | Put the window under `container`, an element of your own, instead of a layer of the root. Null goes back to the layer. The window is built again under the new parent. |
| `void RefreshNow()` | Draw the window now while it is open, instead of waiting for the next frame, for example right after changing what it shows. |
| `protected bool EnsureBuilt()` | Build the window now if it is not on screen yet. True when it is. |
| `protected void Detach()` | Take the window off screen and forget it. |

## VtUnitFramePresenter

Class.

Reads a unit into a `VtUnitFrameState`: name, level, death, every pool, the active buffs folded by definition, and the cast or channel in progress. Bind it to a unit once and read every frame. No UI types, so any view can draw it.

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `VtUnit Unit { get; }` | The unit being read, or null. |
| `void Bind(VtUnit target)` | Read `target` from now on. Null reads nothing. |
| `void Read(VtUnitFrameState state)` | Fill `state` from the bound unit. Clears it when there is none. |
| `static VtCastState ReadCast(VtUnitAbilities abilities)` | The cast or channel `abilities` has in progress, inactive when there is none or `abilities` is null. |

## VtResourceBarPresenter

Class.

Reads one amount of a unit into a `VtResourceBarState`: a pool with its name and numbers, the experience with the level and the numbers or "Max level", or the cast in progress with the ability and the seconds left. Bind it to a unit once and read every frame. No UI types, so any view can draw it.

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `VtUnit Unit { get; }` | The unit being read, or null. |
| `void Bind(VtUnit target)` | Read `target` from now on. Null reads nothing. |
| `void Read(VtResourceBarState state, VtBarSource source, VtResourceKind pool)` | Fill `state` with `source` of the bound unit, `pool` naming the pool for `VtBarSource.Pool`. Clears it when there is nothing to show. |
| `static VtProgressKind KindOf(VtResourceKind kind)` | The bar colour for a pool kind: health, mana, stamina for the stamina-like pools, else the accent. |

## VtXpPresenter

Static class.

Reads a unit's level and experience into a `VtXpState`. A unit without a `VtUnitLevel` reads as its definition's level with no experience.

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `static VtXpState Read(VtUnit unit)` | The state of `unit`. |
| `static VtXpState Read(VtUnit unit, VtUnitLevel level)` | The state of `unit` with its `level` component already looked up. |

## VtActionBarPresenter

Class.

Reads a unit's `VtAbilityHotkeys` into a list of `VtActionSlotState`: the ability, its key, the cooldown with the global cooldown folded in, whether it is affordable and whether it is being aimed. Bind once, read every frame; the list is reused.

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `VtAbilityHotkeys Hotkeys { get; }` | The hotkeys being read, or null. |
| `int SlotCount { get; }` | How many slots the bound hotkeys have. |
| `void Bind(VtAbilityHotkeys target)` | Read `target` from now on. Null reads nothing. |
| `void Read(List<VtActionSlotState> slots)` | Fill `slots` with one entry per hotkey slot. Empties it when nothing is bound. |
| `static string Describe(VtAbilityDefinition ability)` | The cost line for `ability`: "20 MP · 1.5s", "instant", "channel", or empty. |
| `static string Caption(VtAbilityDefinition ability)` | The short line under a slot for `ability`: its cost, "20 MP", or for a free ability its cast, "1.5s", "instant" or "channel". Empty for null. |

## VtStatListPresenter

Static class.

Reads the rows of a stat list off a unit's modifiers and formats their values. No UI types, so any view can draw them.

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `static float Read(VtUnitModifiers modifiers, in VtStatRow row)` | The value of `row` on `modifiers`: the attribute total, the stat's percentage bonus for `VtStatFormat.BonusPercent`, otherwise the stat's flat total. |
| `static void Read(VtUnitModifiers modifiers, VtStatRow[] rows, float[] values)` | Fill `values` with the value of each row. The array must be at least as long as `rows`. |
| `static string Format(VtStatFormat format, float value)` | `value` printed as `format` says: "120", "25%" or "+30%". |

## VtInventoryPresenter

Class.

Reads a unit's bag into a `VtInventoryState`: every entry with its count and durability, whether the unit can put it on and why not, whether it can be used, and the wallet in sort order. Bind it to a unit once and read every frame. No UI types, so any view can draw it.

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `VtUnit Unit { get; }` | The unit being read, or null. |
| `VtUnitInventory Inventory { get; }` | The bag being read, or null when the unit has none. |
| `VtUnitEquipment Equipment { get; }` | The unit's equipment, which decides what can be put on. |
| `VtUnitWallet Wallet { get; }` | The wallet being read, or null when the unit has none. |
| `void Bind(VtUnit target)` | Read `target` from now on. Null reads nothing. |
| `void Read(VtInventoryState state)` | Fill `state` from the bound unit. Clears it when there is none. |
| `static void ReadCurrencies(VtUnitWallet source, List<VtCurrencyState> into)` | Fill `into` with every currency in `source`, lowest sort weight first. A null wallet empties the list. |

Class.

## VtCraftingPresenter

Class.

Reads a unit into a `VtCraftingState`: its crafting skills with level and experience, the recipes it knows plus the ones the window is configured with, every recipe's ingredients against what it carries, why a recipe cannot be crafted, the craft in progress and the station it stands at. Bind it to a unit once and read every frame. No UI types, so any view can draw it.

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `VtUnit Unit { get; }` | The unit being read, or null. |
| `VtUnitCrafter Crafter { get; }` | The unit's crafter, or null when it has none. |

| `bool IsInReach(VtCraftingStation station)` | Whether the unit stands close enough to `station` to use it. |
| `VtCraftingStation NearestStation(VtRecipeStationDefinition type)` | The station of `type` nearest the unit, or null. A null type has no station. |
| `VtCraftingStation StationInReach()` | The nearest station the unit stands at, whatever its type, or null. |
| `void Read(VtCraftingState state)` | Fill `state` from the bound unit. Clears it when there is none. |

## VtBuildPresenter

Class.

The reading side of a build menu: reads a unit into a `VtBuildState` with the category tabs, the pieces in the chosen category, whether each can be built and why not, every cost line against the unit's cost source, and the piece being placed. `Select` starts placing a piece. Bind it to a unit once and read every frame. No UI types, so any view can draw it.

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `VtUnit Unit { get; }` | The unit being read, or null. |
| `VtUnitBuilder Builder { get; }` | The unit's builder, or null when it has none. |
| `List<VtBuildableDefinition> Buildables { get; }` | The pieces the menu lists. Leave it empty to list every buildable in the catalog. |
| `VtDefinitionCatalog Catalog { get; set; }` | The catalog read while `Buildables` is empty. Null uses the shared catalog. |
| `bool FilterByCategory { get; set; }` | Whether the menu shows one category. False lists every piece. |
| `VtBuildableCategoryDefinition Category { get; set; }` | The category shown while `FilterByCategory` is on; null shows the pieces without one. |
| `void Bind(VtUnit target)` | Read `target` from now on. Null reads nothing. |
| `void ShowCategory(VtBuildableCategoryDefinition category)` | Show only `category`; null shows the pieces without one. |
| `void ShowAll()` | Show every piece. |
| `bool Select(VtBuildableDefinition buildable, out VtBuildFailureReason reason)` | Start placing `buildable`. Selecting the piece being placed stops placing it; selecting another switches to it. False with the reason when placement did not start. |
| `void Read(VtBuildState state)` | Fill `state` from the bound unit. Clears it when there is none. |

## VtThreatPresenter

Class.

Reads the threat table a player wants to see into a `VtThreatState`: the table of the unit the viewer has selected, or else of the unit it is fighting, with every attacker sorted from highest threat to lowest and each row's share of the top. Bind it to the viewer once and read every frame. No UI types, so any view can draw it.

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `VtUnit Viewer { get; }` | The unit the list is seen from, or null. |
| `void Bind(VtUnit player)` | Read the table `player` is looking at from now on. Null reads nothing. |
| `VtUnit CurrentTarget()` | The unit whose table the viewer is looking at right now: its selected unit when that unit keeps a threat table, else the unit it is fighting when that one does, else null. |
| `void Read(VtThreatState state)` | Fill `state` from the table the viewer is looking at. Clears it when there is none. |

## VtInteractionPresenter

Class.

Finds the nearest thing a player can right-click — a quest giver, a vendor, a crafting station, a dropped item or a resource node — and describes it for the interaction prompt. Looking for them is a scene scan, so it happens on demand through `Rescan`; `Read` only measures the units found last time, which is cheap enough for every frame.

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `VtUnit Player { get; }` | The player the prompt is for, or null. |
| `float Range { get; set; }` | Metres the prompt reaches, unless the thing itself reaches further. |
| `IReadOnlyList<Component> Found { get; }` | The things found by the last `Rescan`, in the order they were found. |
| `Func<IEnumerable<Component>> Candidates { get; set; }` | The things the prompt considers. Null looks through the scene for the interactables Vantage ships: quest givers, vendors, crafting stations, dropped items and resource nodes. |
| `Func<Component, string> VerbProvider { get; set; }` | The verb for a thing, a localization key. Null uses `DefaultVerb`. |
| `Func<Component, string> NameProvider { get; set; }` | The name of a thing. Null uses `DefaultName`. |
| `void Bind(VtUnit unit)` | Show prompts for `unit` from now on. Null shows nothing. Looks for interactables straight away. |
| `void Rescan()` | Look for interactables again, after spawning or removing one. The prompt does this on a timer of its own; call it to pick up a change in the same frame. |
| `void Read(VtInteractionState state)` | Fill `state` with the nearest thing in range. Clears it when there is none. |
| `static string DefaultVerb(Component target)` | The verb for `target`: talk to a quest giver, trade with a vendor, use a crafting station, gather a resource node and pick up anything else. |
| `static string DefaultName(Component target)` | The name of `target`: the item on a dropped item, the resource on a node, the unit's name on an NPC, and the object's name for anything else. |

## VtMinimapPresenter

Class.

Reads what a minimap shows around a unit into a `VtMinimapState`: the map area it stands in, itself, the units around it by their relation to it, quest givers with something for it, the places and people its active quests send it to, and the `VtMapMarker`s in the scene. Units and markers in the fog of war show by their own rule. No UI types, so any view can draw it.

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `VtUnit Viewer { get; }` | The unit being read, or null. |
| `VtMinimapFilter Filter` | Which markers are read. |
| `Func<Vector3, bool> IsVisible` | Whether a point is in sight. Null asks the scene's `VtFogOfWar`, and everything is in sight without one. |
| `Func<Vector3, bool> IsExplored` | Whether a point has been seen. Null asks the scene's `VtFogOfWar`, and everything has been seen without one. |
| `void Bind(VtUnit unit)` | Read around `unit` from now on. Null reads nothing. |
| `void Read(VtMinimapState state)` | Fill `state` around the bound unit. Clears it when there is none. |

## VtTooltipContent

Class.

What a tooltip shows, with no UI types: a title, a subtitle, label and value rows and free lines. `VtItemTooltip` and `VtAbilityTooltip` build one from a definition; a tooltip element draws it. Reuse an instance with `Clear` to avoid allocations.

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `bool IsEmpty { get; }` | Whether there is anything to show. |
| `string Title` | The title, a localization key or the text itself. |
| `string Subtitle` | The muted line under the title, such as a rarity or a targeting mode. |
| `readonly List<VtTooltipRow> Rows` | Label and value rows, shown before the lines. |
| `readonly List<VtTooltipLine> Lines` | Free lines, shown after the rows. |
| `VtTooltipContent Clear()` | Forget everything. |
| `VtTooltipContent Row(string label, string value, VtTooltipLineKind kind = VtTooltipLineKind.Normal)` | Add a label and value row. |
| `VtTooltipContent Line(string text, VtTooltipLineKind kind = VtTooltipLineKind.Normal)` | Add a line. |

## VtAbilityTooltip

Static class.

Builds the tooltip of an ability: its name, how it targets, the cost, cast time, cooldown, range and area, what its effects do, such as "Damage 40 – 55 Fire" or "Applies Burning", and its description. No UI types; a tooltip element draws the result.

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `static void RegisterEffect<T>(Action<T, VtTooltipContent> describe)` | Describe effects of type `T` with `describe`, which adds rows or lines to the tooltip being built. Registering a type again replaces the first describer. |
| `static VtTooltipContent Build(VtAbilityDefinition ability, VtTooltipContent content)` | Fill `content` for `ability`. A null ability clears it. |
| `static string CastText(VtAbilityDefinition ability)` | The cast column: "Instant", "1.5 s" or "Channel 4 s". |
| `static string TargetingKey(VtTargetingMode mode)` | The localization key naming `mode`. |
| `static string DamageText(int min, int max, VtDamageType type)` | A damage roll as "40 – 55 Fire", or "40 Fire" when the two ends meet. |

## VtItemTooltip

Static class.

Builds the tooltip of an item: its name, rarity and slot, every stat and attribute bonus, the set it belongs to with the pieces worn, its requirements marked when the viewer does not meet them, what using it does, its value and its description. No UI types; a tooltip element draws the result.

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `static VtTooltipContent Build(VtItemDefinition item, VtUnit viewer, VtTooltipContent content)` | Fill `content` for `item` as seen by `viewer`, which may be null. With a viewer, unmet requirements read as bad and the set line counts the pieces worn. |
| `static string Subtitle(VtItemDefinition item)` | The rarity and the slot, joined with a dot, or whichever the item has. |
| `static string SlotName(VtEquipmentSlot slot)` | An equipment slot as words: "Main hand", "Ring 1". |

## VtBuffTooltip

Static class.

Builds the tooltip of a buff on a unit: its name, the stacks, the time left, every stat and attribute it changes, what it does each tick, and its description. No UI types; a tooltip element draws the result.

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `static VtTooltipContent Build(in VtBuffState buff, VtTooltipContent content)` | Fill `content` for `buff` as a unit carries it. A buff without a definition clears it. |

## VtTooltips

Static class.

The one tooltip a screen shows, and the wiring that puts it up. Give `Host` the `VtTooltip` sitting on the tooltip layer, then hand any element a source of content with `Attach`: the tooltip follows the pointer and the focus, so a player on a gamepad reads the same text as a player on a mouse.

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `static VtTooltip Host { get; set; }` | The tooltip every call goes to, normally the one on the tooltip layer. Null means no tooltips. |
| `static int DelayMs` | How long the pointer or the focus rests on an element before its tooltip goes up, in milliseconds. |
| `static void Attach(VisualElement element, Func<VtTooltipContent> source, VtTooltipPlacement placement = VtTooltipPlacement.Element)` | Show the tooltip for `element` after the delay whenever the pointer or the focus reaches it, and take it down when they leave. `source` is asked each time, so it can read live numbers; handing back null or an empty content shows nothing. `placement` puts the tooltip under the element, or under the pointer and following it. Attaching twice replaces the first source. |
| `static void Detach(VisualElement element)` | Stop showing a tooltip for `element`. |
| `static bool IsAttached(VisualElement element)` | Whether `element` has a tooltip source on it. |
| `static void ShowNow(VisualElement anchor, VtTooltipContent content)` | Put `content` up next to `anchor` right away, without the delay, for a key press or a selection that should explain itself at once. Nothing to show takes the tooltip down. |
| `static void ShowAtPointer(Vector2 panelPosition, VtTooltipContent content)` | Put `content` up under the pointer at `panelPosition`, in panel coordinates as pointer events report them, right away. It flips above near the bottom of the screen and slides left at the right edge. Nothing to show takes the tooltip down. |
| `static void Hide()` | Take the tooltip down. |

## VtTheme

Static class.

Switches the Vantage theme at runtime. Each option is a class on the element you pass, normally `UIDocument.rootVisualElement`, and the Vantage theme style sheet redefines the `--vt-` colour, radius and font variables for that class, so everything under the element follows.

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `const string TypefacePrefix` | Start of every typeface class name. |
| `const string InterTypeface` | The Inter typeface, the default. |
| `static string ClassName(VtThemeMode mode)` | The class for `mode`. |
| `static string ClassName(VtThemeAccent accent)` | The class for `accent`. |
| `static string ClassName(VtThemeRadius radius)` | The class for `radius`. |
| `static void SetMode(VisualElement root, VtThemeMode mode)` | Use `mode` for everything under `root`. |
| `static void SetAccent(VisualElement root, VtThemeAccent accent)` | Use `accent` for everything under `root`. |
| `static void SetRadius(VisualElement root, VtThemeRadius radius)` | Use `radius` for everything under `root`. |
| `static void SetTypeface(VisualElement root, string typefaceClass)` | Use the typeface class `typefaceClass`, replacing any other typeface class. Null or empty goes back to Inter. |
| `static VtThemeMode GetMode(VisualElement root)` | The mode set on `root`, Dark when none is. |
| `static VtThemeAccent GetAccent(VisualElement root)` | The accent set on `root`, Neutral when none is. |
| `static VtThemeRadius GetRadius(VisualElement root)` | The radius set on `root`, Medium when none is. |
| `static string GetTypeface(VisualElement root)` | The typeface class set on `root`, `InterTypeface` when none is. |

## VtUiStates

Static class.

The state classes every Vantage component and every panel of your own shares, so one rule in the theme styles selected and disabled-looking elements wherever they appear: chips, rows, buttons and list entries.

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `const string SelectedUssClassName` | Class on a chosen chip, row, button or entry. |
| `const string DisabledUssClassName` | Class on an element that should look unavailable. |
| `static void SetSelected(VisualElement element, bool selected)` | Add or remove `SelectedUssClassName` on `element`. |
| `static void SetDisabledLook(VisualElement element, bool disabled)` | Add or remove `DisabledUssClassName` on `element`. |

## VtIcons

Static class.

Where `VtIcon` and every Vantage component look an icon id up. The shipped `Resources/VtIconSet` holds the Lucide glyphs the package uses. `Install` puts your own `VtIconSet` in front of it: ids it has win, ids it lacks fall through to the shipped set, so you can replace one glyph or add a hundred without copying the rest.

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `static VtIconSet Installed { get; }` | The set installed with `Install`, or null when the shipped set is the only one. |
| `static VtIconSet Shipped { get; }` | The shipped set, loaded from Resources on first use. Null when it is missing. |
| `static event Action OnChanged` | Fires after `Install`. Icons on screen redraw here. |
| `const string ResourcePath` | Resources path of the shipped icon set. |
| `static void Install(VtIconSet set)` | Look ids up in `set` before the shipped set. Null goes back to the shipped set alone. |
| `static bool TryGet(string id, out Background background)` | The image for `id`: from the installed set and its fallbacks, else the shipped set. |
| `static bool Contains(string id)` | Whether any set has an icon called `id`. |
| `static void ResetCache()` | Forget the loaded and the installed set, going back to the shipped set alone. |

## VtUiLayouts

Static class.

Default layouts for panels built on `VtHudPanel`, one UXML file each under any `Resources/VtLayouts` folder. A panel clones its layout and finds its parts by name, so a layout of your own with the same names, set on the panel's **Layout** field, changes how the panel is arranged without any code.

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `static VisualTreeAsset Load(string name)` | The layout called `name` under `Resources/VtLayouts`, or null with one warning when it is missing. |
| `static VisualElement Instantiate(VisualTreeAsset layout)` | Clone `layout` and hand back its root element: the single top-level element of the file, or the whole clone when the file has several. Null for a null layout. |
| `static void ResetCache()` | Forget the loaded layouts, so the next `Load` reads each file again. |

## VtIconEntry

Serializable class.

One icon in a `VtIconSet`: an id and the image drawn for it.

### Inspector fields

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Id (`id`) | `string` | Empty | The name UI refers to the icon by, such as 'chevron-down'. |
| Vector (`vector`) | `VectorImage` | None | A vector image, tinted by the UI. Used when set. |
| Sprite (`sprite`) | `Sprite` | None | A sprite, used when there is no vector image. |

## Enums

### VtUiLayer

The layers of a screen, from the back to the front.

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `World` | Things anchored to the world: nameplates, interaction prompts, markers. |
| `Hud` | The HUD: frames, bars, action bar, quest tracker. |
| `Windows` | Windows opened while playing: inventory, quest log, crafting. |
| `Menus` | Menus that take over: the game menu, settings. |
| `Overlays` | Overlays on top of everything: dialogs, toasts, the death screen. |
| `Tooltip` | The tooltip, always in front. |

### VtUiRegion

A place on the HUD layer for panels that just need a corner or an edge.

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `TopLeft` | Top left corner, stacking down. |
| `TopCenter` | Top edge, centred. |
| `TopRight` | Top right corner, stacking down. |
| `BottomLeft` | Bottom left corner, stacking up. |
| `BottomCenter` | Bottom edge, centred. |
| `BottomRight` | Bottom right corner, stacking up. |

### VtMapMarkerTint

Which colour a `VtMapMarker` takes on the minimap.

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `Foreground` | The text colour. |
| `Muted` | The secondary text colour. |
| `Primary` | The accent. |
| `Quest` | The quest colour. |
| `Hostile` | The hostile colour. |
| `Friendly` | The friendly colour. |
| `Neutral` | The neutral colour. |

### VtMapMarkerReveal

When a `VtMapMarker` shows through the fog of war.

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `Always` | Always, fog or not. |
| `WhenExplored` | Once the player has seen the spot. |
| `WhenVisible` | Only while the spot is in sight. |

### VtBarSource

What a resource bar reads from its unit.

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `Pool` | One of the unit's resource pools: health, mana, stamina and the rest. |
| `Experience` | The unit's experience towards its next level. |
| `Cast` | The cast or channel in progress. The bar is empty while nothing is cast. |

### VtResourceKind

The kind of a resource pool on a unit, such as health, mana, stamina or rage. A unit definition lists the pools it has; read one with `VtUnitStats.GetPool`.

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `HP` | Health. The unit dies when it reaches 0. |
| `MP` | Mana, spent by spells. |
| `Stamina` | Stamina, spent by physical actions such as sprinting or dodging. |
| `Rage` | Rage, built by dealing and taking damage rather than regenerating. |
| `Focus` | Focus, a small fast-refilling pool for ranged or precise actions. |
| `Energy` | Energy, a fixed-size pool that refills quickly. |
| `ComboPoints` | Combo points, built by some abilities and spent by finishers. |
| `Charges` | Charges, discrete uses that refill one at a time. |
| `Hunger` | Food pool: decreases over time, damages HP when empty. |
| `Thirst` | Water pool: decreases over time, damages HP when empty. |
| `Shield` | Secondary HP layer — sci-fi / mage-barrier style. Regenerates out of combat (per the configured `VtRegenMode`); takes damage before HP only when consumer code wires that interception (typically via an `VtUnitStats.OnPreTakeDamage` hook). Pair with `stat.max_shield` / `stat.shield_regen`. |

### VtProgressKind

The colour of a `VtProgressBar`'s fill.

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `Primary` | The accent colour. The default. |
| `Health` | The health colour. |
| `Mana` | The mana colour. |
| `Stamina` | The stamina colour. |
| `Experience` | The experience colour. |
| `Cast` | The cast colour, for a cast or channel in progress. |

### VtStatFormat

How a stat list prints a value.

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `Flat` | The flat total, such as armor 120. |
| `FlatAsPercent` | The flat total read as a fraction, such as crit chance 0.25 shown as 25%. |
| `BonusPercent` | The percentage bonus, such as physical power +30%. |

### VtEquipmentSlot

The set of equipment slots an item can occupy on a unit. Used as the key for the slot map on `VtUnitEquipment` and as the source-id suffix when equipped items push their modifiers / attributes / traits (`"equipment_<slot>"`).

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `None` | Inventory-only / non-equippable. Potions, materials, quest items. |
| `Head` | Helm / hat / hood. |
| `Chest` | Chestpiece / robe / breastplate. |
| `Legs` | Leg armor / pants / greaves. |
| `Feet` | Boots / sandals / sabatons. |
| `Hands` | Gloves / gauntlets / bracers. |
| `MainHand` | Primary weapon. 2H weapons occupy this slot and block `OffHand`. |
| `OffHand` | Off-hand weapon, shield, or focus. Auto-unequipped when a 2H is equipped to `MainHand`. |
| `Neck` | Necklace / amulet / pendant. |
| `Ring1` | First ring slot. Members of the Ring family. |
| `Ring2` | Second ring slot. Members of the Ring family. |
| `Trinket1` | First trinket slot. Members of the Trinket family. |
| `Trinket2` | Second trinket slot. Members of the Trinket family. |
| `Back` | Worn on the back: backpack, cloak, quiver. |

### VtBuildFailureReason

Why a builder call was refused or a placement is invalid.

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `None` | Nothing refused: the call succeeded or the placement is valid. |
| `BuildableNull` | No buildable was given, or it has no prefab. |
| `MissingItems` | The builder cannot pay the buildable's item cost. |
| `MissingCurrency` | The builder cannot pay the buildable's currency cost. |
| `MissingRequiredItems` | The builder does not carry the buildable's required items, such as a hammer. |
| `LevelTooLow` | The builder's level is below the buildable's required level. |
| `MissingPrereqQuests` | A quest the buildable requires has not been turned in. |
| `BlockedByCollider` | A collider on the buildable's forbidden overlap layers is in the way. |
| `NoSurface` | The cursor points at no surface the piece can stand on. |
| `AlreadyPlacing` | A placement is already in progress. |
| `NotPlacing` | Nothing is being placed. |
| `AuthorityNotLocal` | This copy is not the authority. `VtUnitBuilder.TryPlace` and `VtUnitBuilder.TryDemolish` send the request to the authority, which decides. |
| `NoBuilderComponent` | The unit has no builder component. |
| `NotABuildable` | The target of a demolish is not something this system placed. |
| `CrossesCliff` | The footprint spans more than one cliff level or lies on a ramp. |
| `OutOfRange` | The placement point is farther from the builder than the buildable's placement range. |
| `Locked` | The buildable's `VtBuildableDefinition.requiredUnlock` is not owned. |
| `BlockedGround` | The footprint covers a cell the cliff map marks as blocked. |
| `RefusedByRule` | A placement rule refused. `VtBuildRefusal.RuleKey` carries the rule's own reason. |

### VtTooltipLineKind

How a tooltip line reads.

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `Normal` | Plain text. |
| `Muted` | Secondary text, such as flavour or a hint. |
| `Good` | Something in the player's favour, such as a bonus. |
| `Bad` | Something against the player, such as an unmet requirement. |

### VtTargetingMode

How an `VtAbilityDefinition` picks its target.

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `Self` | No target — the ability affects the caster directly. |
| `SingleTarget` | A single `IVtAttackable`. Most melee / single-shot ranged abilities. |
| `GroundPoint` | A world-space point. Ground-targeted AoE (meteor strike, blizzard, healing circle). |

### VtDamageType

The *element* of an attack — routed through the corresponding `resistX` stat on `VtCoreStats` in `VtUnitStats.TakeDamage`.

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `Physical` | Weapons, claws and falling rocks. Reduced by armor; resisted by stat.resist_physical. |
| `Fire` | Fire and burning. Resisted by stat.resist_fire. |
| `Cold` | Frost and ice. Resisted by stat.resist_cold. |
| `Poison` | Poison and venom, often dealt over time. Resisted by stat.resist_poison. |
| `True` | Bypasses all mitigation (resistance, armor, matrix). Use sparingly. |
| `Lightning` | Electricity / chain-lightning / EMP-flavor. Resisted by stat.resist_lightning. |
| `Holy` | Paladin / priest school. Strong vs undead in many genres. Resisted by stat.resist_holy. |
| `Shadow` | Warlock / necromancer school — corruption, agony, void. Resisted by stat.resist_shadow. Often paired oppositionally with Holy. |
| `Arcane` | Mage's "raw magic" school — distinct from elemental. Magic missile, polymorph. Resisted by stat.resist_arcane. Conventionally hardest to resist. |
| `Nature` | Druid / shaman school — earth, plant, weather, wildlife. Resisted by stat.resist_nature. |

### VtTooltipPlacement

Where a tooltip goes relative to the element it explains.

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `Element` | Under the element, lined up with its left edge. The default. |
| `Pointer` | Under the pointer, following it while it moves over the element. Focus from a gamepad or the keyboard has no pointer, so it falls back to the element. |

| `Dark` | Dark surfaces with light text. The default. |
| `Light` | Light surfaces with dark text. |
